notes: Only the author of the Sanskrit original, Kalyāṇamalla (mahākavi), is named. "mallāḍa ṣāna vinodāya" is probably a patron-phrase, i.e. Lāḍakhān (Lād Khān) as the one for whose amusement the work was written, in the title phrase "śrīmallāḍa ṣāna vinodāya". Not listed as a person: the reading is uncertain, and the same phrase is a standard part of the Anaṅgaraṅga's own text, not the copy's production. Scribe, donor and king are not named; the ++++ lacunae may have hidden a scribe name. Era is not stated. 1005 is probably VS (≈ 948 CE) or ŚS, but both are implausible for Kalyāṇamalla, who wrote in the 16th century. It may instead be a corrupt or later NS/VS date, so ce_approx is left empty. The Nepali-language gloss (bhāṣā vyākhyāna) is anonymous.
